title_en: Wanshun Company v. Yongxin Company et al. — dispute over cooperative development agreement
ruling_gist_en: 1. The party that urges the other party to perform shall be the non-breaching party. A party in breach does not have the right to rescind the contract arising from the other party's failure to perform after being urged.
keywords_en: Civil; Dispute over Cooperative Development Agreement; Second Instance; Supreme People's Court; Shanghai; Zhejiang; Hong Kong Special Administrative Region; Legal Person; Contract Law; Conditions for Vesting of Right to Rescind Contract; Qualifications of Party Urging Performance; Legal Effects of Contract Rescission; Affirm Original Judgment; Cooperative Development Agreement; Transfer of Land Use Rights; Urging Performance; Good Faith; Dispute over Cooperative Development Agreement Involving New Company, etc.
full_text_en:
Wanshun Company v. Yongxin Company et al. — Dispute over Cooperation Development Agreement

Ruling Summary

1. The party urging the other party to perform shall be the observant party; a party in breach of contract does not enjoy the right to rescind the contract based on the other party's continued non-performance following a notice.

2. The exercise of the right to rescind a contract is conditional upon the fulfillment of the conditions for rescission, and the rescission must comply with the procedures prescribed by law; otherwise, it cannot produce the legal effect of contract rescission.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2003) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 47

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Shanghai Wanshun Real Estate Development Company, domiciled at No. 388 Renmin Road, Shanghai.

Legal Representative: Wang Xuyang, General Manager.

Agent ad litem: Xue Xiaojian, attorney at Beijing Lutong United Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhu Ping, attorney at Shanghai United Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Yongxin Industrial Development Co., Ltd. (NOVEL INDUSTRIES COMPANY LIMITED), domiciled at 12th Floor, Yongxin Industrial Building, No. 850-870 Lai Chi Kok Road, Cheung Sha Wan, Kowloon, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Legal Representative: Cao Qidong, Director.

Agent ad litem: Cui Guofu, male, born August 8, 1945, address: 15th Floor, Reform Monthly Bulletin Building, No. 60 Simadu Lane, Zhonghe Road, Hangzhou City, Zhejiang Province.

Agent ad litem: Lai Guilan, attorney at Zhejiang Hanting Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Yiwu Yongxin Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 10 Huagong Road, Yiwu City, Zhejiang Province.

Legal Representative: He Zhiqiang, General Manager.

Dissatisfied with the civil judgment (1998) Zhe Fa Min Chu Zi No. 2 rendered by the Zhejiang High People's Court in the dispute over cooperation development agreement, the appellant Shanghai Wanshun Real Estate Development Company appealed to this Court. On December 14, 2000, this Court issued a civil ruling (2000) Min Zhong Zi No. 62 remanding the case for retrial. During the retrial proceedings, the Zhejiang High People's Court, on May 15, 2001, added Yiwu Yongxin Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. as a third party, and on May 6, 2003, rendered the civil judgment (2000) Zhe Fa Min Chong Chu Zi No. 2. The appellant Shanghai Wanshun Real Estate Development Company appealed against that judgment to this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing on August 12, 2003. The agents ad litem of the appellant Shanghai Wanshun Real Estate Development Company, Xue Xiaojian and Zhu Ping, the agent ad litem of the appellee Yongxin Industrial Development Co., Ltd., Lai Guilan, and the legal representative of the original third party Yiwu Yongxin Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., He Zhiqiang, appeared in court for the proceedings. The case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found through trial that on February 7, 1993, Yongxin Industrial Development Co., Ltd. (formerly known as Yongxin Technology Development Co., Ltd. and Yongxin Investment and Trade Co., Ltd., renamed Yongxin Industrial Development Co., Ltd. on January 4, 1996, hereinafter collectively referred to as Yongxin Company) signed the "Memorandum of Consultation on the Implementation of the Letter of Intent for Economic and Technical Cooperation" with the Yiwu Municipal Government. The main contents were: 1. Concerning the relocation and renovation of Yiwu Paper Mill and real estate development. The Yiwu side endorsed the idea proposed by Yongxin Company that "in accordance with the overall urban planning requirements, most of the existing plant area of Yiwu Paper Mill should be developed into a park with distinctive local characteristics and a modern urban atmosphere, similar to Taikoo Shing in Hong Kong, which would be publicly offered for merchant attraction and auctioned. Most of the funds from the land use rights merchant attraction and auction would be used to support Yiwu Paper Mill in adjusting its product structure and undertaking other industrial projects, while a small portion would be used as start-up capital for real estate development, integrating the two aspects for comprehensive consideration." 2. The Yiwu side expressed great interest in the color printing, packaging, and vacuum aluminum plating projects proposed by Yongxin Company and would form a special team as soon as possible to conduct necessary research and analysis on the product direction, scale, and market prospects of the above three projects. Then, based on market conditions and financial strength, one or two projects would be selected for joint development through a joint venture. Yongxin Company would be responsible for technology and equipment introduction for the selected projects, and the form of the joint venture and capital contribution ratios would be further negotiated at that time. 3. Yongxin Company suggested that the Yiwu side directly contact Yongxin Company through a comprehensive industrial company for implementation and requested that the municipal government provide strong policy support. The Yiwu side agreed to study the matter and implement it as soon as possible. On March 31, 1993, the account number 115014906288 of Shaoxing Light Textiles remitted RMB 10 million to Yiwu Velvet Chemical General Plant. On April 12, Yiwu Velvet Chemical General Plant remitted RMB 10 million to Shanghai Wanshun Real Estate Development Company (hereinafter referred to as Wanshun Company). On April 14, Wanshun Company remitted RMB 10 million to the Beijing Office of Yongxin Company. On April 23, Nanhui Agricultural Bank remitted RMB 10 million to Yiwu Agricultural Bank. On April 26, Yiwu Agricultural Bank remitted RMB 10 million to Yiwu Velvet Chemical General Plant. On April 27, Yiwu Velvet Chemical General Plant remitted RMB 10 million to Wanshun Company. On April 28, Yiwu Municipal Government (Party A) and Yongxin Company (Party B) signed an agreement, stipulating: 1. The state-owned land use rights of approximately 80,000 square meters originally allocated gratuitously to Yiwu Paper Mill (specific location and exact area to be determined based on planning drawings) would be recovered by Party A and transferred by agreement to Party B at a preferential price for the development of commercial and residential buildings. The term of the land use rights transfer was to be determined in accordance with national regulations. 2. The land transfer price was RMB 650,000 per mu. Upon signing the agreement, Party B paid a deposit of RMB 10 million. Within three months from the date of signing the contract, an additional RMB 2 million was to be paid. The remaining land price was to be fully paid within seven months from the date of signing. 3. Party B was to bear the costs of leveling the land, providing water, electricity, and roads, as well as greening and community road construction within the transferred plot. Party B was fully responsible for the construction of the Worker's Road section. For the Huagong Road and Yidong Road sections adjacent to the original paper mill, Party B was to bear half of the construction costs. The costs for increasing the water and electricity capacity within the community were to be borne by Party B. 4. Party A guaranteed that within five months after the formal execution of the land transfer contract, it would complete the demolition and relocation of all buildings, structures, and equipment within the transferred land. 5. Party B was to prepare a detailed plan for the community's high-rise buildings based on the community planning points and relevant indicators provided by Party A, which could only be implemented after approval by Party A. 6. The two parties jointly invested in establishing a first-class printing enterprise with a total investment of no less than RMB 40 million. The investment ratio was tentatively set at 70% for Party A and 30% for Party B. Both parties would work together to complete construction and commence production within two years. If, due to Party B's fault, the joint venture project failed to materialize, the land transfer price would be calculated at RMB 850,000 per mu, and only after Party B had paid the full land price calculated on this basis would Party A handle the relevant procedures for the transfer of real estate. If, due to Party A's fault, losses were caused to Party B, Party A was to provide compensation. 7. Workers needed by the new joint venture enterprise were to be selected first from the original employees of the paper mill. The US dollars required for the new printing equipment were to be arranged by Party B. On May 4 of the same year, Yongxin Company (Party A) and Wanshun Company (Party B) signed an agreement, stipulating: 1. Party A was responsible for entering into a contract with the Yiwu Land Administration Bureau for the transfer of the state-owned land use rights of approximately 80,000 square meters of the original Yiwu Paper Mill in accordance with the "Trial Measures for the Paid Transfer and Assignment of Urban State-Owned Land Use Rights" of Yiwu City and relevant national laws and regulations. Party A was also to establish a real estate development company under its own name for this project in Yiwu. 2. Party A was responsible for handling all preliminary procedures with the relevant authorities of Yiwu City in the real estate development of this project and coordinating any issues that arose. 3. Party B was responsible for raising funds and, in accordance with the contract and related agreements signed between Party A and the Yiwu Land Administration Bureau, paying the full land price (payment method to follow the time stipulated in the relevant contract). 4. Party B was to bear, in accordance with relevant regulations, the costs of leveling the land, providing water, electricity, and roads, as well as greening and community road construction within the transferred plot, and the costs of increasing water and electricity capacity. 5. Party B was to prepare a detailed plan for the community's high-rise buildings based on the community planning points and relevant indicators provided by the Yiwu Land Administration Bureau, which could only be implemented after approval by the relevant authorities of Yiwu City. 6. In accordance with the agreement between Party A and the municipal government, Party A would hold a 30% stake in the newly established printing enterprise (with a total investment of over RMB 40 million), with an investment of approximately RMB 15 million. This amount was to be included in the land cost of the real estate project. 7. Within the real estate company registered by Party A, Party B was to send personnel to participate in management and be fully responsible for financial work. 8. The profit from the real estate development project was to be distributed between Party A and Party B, with Party A receiving 60% and Party B receiving 40%. The agreement stated that it would have legal effect upon signing by both parties, and neither party could breach it. On the same day, Yongxin Company paid a deposit of RMB 10 million to the Yiwu Land Administration Bureau. Subsequently, Wanshun Company assigned Lou Renyao and Zhang Qizhen to participate in the daily management of Yiwu Yongxin Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (established on June 23, 1994, with the approval document Waimao Zi Zhe Fu Zi (1993) No. 5595 of the People's Government of Zhejiang Province. The business license was issued on December 15, 1993, indicating the enterprise type as wholly foreign-owned, registered capital of USD 3 million, General Manager He Zhiqiang, Deputy General Manager Jia Sandi. Prior to its establishment, the preparatory office of Yiwu Hong Kong City Real Estate Development Company was formed, hereinafter collectively referred to as Yiwu Yongxin Company). Lou Renyao and Zhang Qizhen were appointed as consultants to Yiwu Yongxin Company; Zhang Qizhen served as Sales Manager and received a salary from Yiwu Yongxin Company. Yu Jianjun served as Deputy General Manager, overseeing the office and finance department, and concurrently held the positions of Office Director and Finance Manager. Yiwu Yongxin Company began collecting advance payments for housing in May of the same year. On June 10 of the same year, Yongxin Company and Wanshun Company signed a supplementary agreement, stipulating: 1. Clause 6 of the main agreement was amended to read: Party A's 30% stake in the newly established printing enterprise (with a total investment of over RMB 40 million) was to be calculated based on 30% of the actual investment, but capped at RMB 15 million, which was to be included in the land cost. 2. The profit distribution in Clause 8 of the main agreement was amended to read: Party A 55%, Party B 45%. The supplementary agreement also stated that it would have the same legal effect as the main agreement. On August 2 of the same year, the Yiwu Land Administration Bureau (Party A) and Yiwu Yongxin Company (Party B) signed the State-Owned Land Use Rights Transfer Contract No. 34 (1993), stipulating: 1. The transferred land was located at No. 10 Huagong Road (the original site of Yiwu Paper Mill), with an area of 121.5 mu. The land was to be used for commercial, service, and residential comprehensive development, with a land use term of 70 years for residential land and 50 years for commercial and service land. The project was to be completed by the end of June 1996. 2. The transfer price for the land use rights was RMB 650,000 per mu, totaling RMB 78.975 million. Upon signing the contract, Party B was required to pay a deposit of RMB 10 million. Within two months from the date of signing, Party B was to pay another RMB 20 million. The remaining land price was to be fully paid within six months from the date of signing. If payment was not made in full within the time limit, Party A had the right to rescind the contract, forfeit the deposit, and claim damages for breach of contract. 3. Party B was to bear the costs of telecommunications, power supply, water supply, drainage, greening, and roads within the transferred plot. The road construction of the Worker's Road section crossing the original paper mill site was to be carried out by Party B in accordance with urban construction planning requirements, with all costs borne by Party B (including water supply and drainage, sewage, cable telecommunications, road lighting, and greening fees) and subject to acceptance according to construction procedures. For the Huagong Road, Yidong Road, and planned 10-meter road (unnamed) sections adjacent to the transferred plot, Party B was to bear half of the road construction costs. The costs of increasing water and electricity capacity within the transferred plot were to be borne by Party B. 4. Party A guaranteed that within five months after the formal signing of the contract, it would complete the demolition and relocation of all buildings and their accessories within the transferred plot. On August 4, 1993, Wanshun Company remitted RMB 112,800 to Yiwu Yongxin Company. On August 7, Yiwu Yongxin Company, upon the instruction of Wanshun Company, paid RMB 10 million and interest of RMB 105,600 to Yiwu Agricultural Bank, with a balance of RMB 7,200 returned to Wanshun Company. On June 28, 1994, Wanshun Company issued a receipt acknowledging receipt of the RMB 7,200. On August 12 and November 8, 1993, Yiwu Yongxin Company paid land transfer fees of RMB 5.4 million and RMB 12.6 million respectively. On November 18 of the same year, Yiwu Yongxin Company borrowed RMB 6 million from Shanghai Yangming Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yangming Company) through Wanshun Company. On December 18, 24, 28, and 31 of the same year, Yiwu Yongxin Company paid Yangming Company, the Jinhua Agricultural Bank International Business Department, and Yiwu Garment Company sums of RMB 710,000, RMB 290,000, RMB 2 million, and RMB 3 million, totaling RMB 6 million, thereby settling the debt to Yangming Company. On January 13, 1994, Yiwu Yongxin Company paid interest of RMB 200,000 to Wanshun Company. On January 28, 1994, the Yiwu Audit Firm issued a capital verification report for Yiwu Yongxin Company, stating that the investor had remitted RMB 10 million from Beijing Yongxin Company to the China Construction Bank Yiwu Sub-branch on April 22, 1993, as operating funds. The capital verification report concluded that the actual paid-in capital of Yiwu Yongxin Company was RMB 10 million. On April 1, 1994, He Zhiqiang, acting on behalf of Yongxin Company, sent a letter to Wanshun Company (hereinafter referred to as the "April 1 Letter"), the main contents of which were: 1. In accordance with Clause 3 of the agreement dated May 4, 1993, Wanshun Company was required to pay the full land transfer fee of RMB 78.975 million and various expenses for leveling the land, providing water, electricity, and roads, totaling over RMB 8 million, within six months (from August 2, 1993 to February 1, 1994). 2. Wanshun Company's failure to perform the agreement had caused great difficulties and had a negative impact on its reputation. The Yiwu Municipal Government had repeatedly urged that the process be accelerated, and the majority of housing purchasers urgently demanded an early start of construction. Yongxin Company had repeatedly urged Wanshun Company to remit the funds, but Wanshun Company had consistently failed to fulfill the agreement. The letter requested that the above-mentioned payments be remitted to Yiwu Yongxin Company by the 15th of that month. If the funds were not remitted to the designated bank on time, the letter would be considered as Wanshun Company's automatic rescission of the agreement. On April 5, May 20, June 3, September 26, 1994, and July 7, 1998, Yiwu Yongxin Company paid land transfer fees of RMB 10 million, RMB 10 million, RMB 20 million, RMB 9.22 million, and RMB 318,133 respectively. On September 6, 1999, Zhu Hai, former Director of the Yiwu Land Administration Bureau, confirmed that Yiwu Yongxin Company had paid the deposit of RMB 10 million for the land transfer fee and had generally made the second installment payment on time. Subsequently, Yiwu Yongxin Company pointed out that part of the transferred land area was occupied by public buildings and requested a re-measurement of the area before paying the full transfer fee. After the Land Administration Bureau verified the area and confirmed the fact, it did not pursue liability for breach of contract regarding the delayed payment of the transfer fee.

Wanshun Company filed a lawsuit, alleging: The cooperation agreement between the parties was lawful and valid and, once signed, should be strictly performed. Wanshun Company had made the initial investment of RMB 10 million and dispatched sales managers, accountants, and cashiers. After the entire plot entered the development and construction phase, revenue from pre-sale housing was substantial, and there were sufficient funds to pay the land price and fund the development and construction. At a time when Wanshun Company had paid the investment funds in accordance with the agreement and the parties were cooperating to achieve results, Yongxin Company attempted to tear up the contract and unilaterally appropriate the profits, an act that violated the law and infringed upon Wanshun Company's lawful rights and interests. Wanshun Company therefore requested the court of first instance to order Yongxin Company to pay 45% of the cooperation development profit, amounting to RMB 16.25 million (amended to RMB 26.17 million during trial), and to bear the litigation costs.

Yongxin Company defended, arguing: 1. The cooperation development agreement and supplementary agreement signed on May 4 and June 10, 1993, represented the true intention of the parties, had lawful content, and should be confirmed as valid. After signing the agreement, Yongxin Company had performed all its obligations in accordance with the agreement, whereas Wanshun Company, apart from remitting RMB 10 million to the Beijing Office of Yongxin Company before the cooperation began, had failed to pay the land transfer fee as agreed and had not borne the costs of leveling the land, providing water, electricity, and roads, or the costs of increasing water and electricity capacity in the development project, thereby constituting a fundamental breach of contract. 2. On April 1, 1994, Yongxin Company sent a letter notifying Wanshun Company that if the amounts payable were not remitted to Yiwu Yongxin Company by April 15, it would be deemed that Wanshun Company had automatically rescinded the agreement. Wanshun Company still failed to perform its corresponding obligations, and therefore the cooperation agreement had been rescinded. 3. Wanshun Company did not file the lawsuit until December 1998, which exceeded the statute of limitations, and therefore it no longer had the right to claim. The RMB 10 million remitted by Wanshun Company to the Beijing Office of Yongxin Company on April 22, 1993, had already been transferred through Yiwu Agricultural Bank on August 7 of the same year. Wanshun Company no longer had any capital investment, and the legal basis for its right to profit distribution under the agreement had been lost. Yongxin Company therefore requested that the court dismiss Wanshun Company's claims and order it to bear the litigation costs.

Yiwu Yongxin Company defended, arguing: Yiwu Yongxin Company was a wholly foreign-owned enterprise established by Yongxin Company. According to the agreement between Wanshun Company and Yongxin Company, Wanshun Company was obligated to raise funds, and therefore the registered capital of Yiwu Yongxin Company should be raised by Wanshun Company. However, apart from the RMB 10 million remitted on April 14, 1993, Wanshun Company had made no other capital contributions. On August 7, 1993, Wanshun Company had already requested Yiwu Yongxin Company to remit the RMB 10 million and interest of RMB 105,600 to its designated account. This RMB 10 million had only been in the project company for three months. Since then, Wanshun Company had made no further capital contributions, and all obligations under the original agreement, including the payment of land transfer fees, were performed by Yongxin Company and Yiwu Yongxin Company. Accordingly, Wanshun Company's unilateral withdrawal of the RMB 10 million and interest was, from Yongxin Company's perspective, tantamount to a withdrawal of investment or an early recovery of investment. With respect to the entire project, Wanshun Company should no longer enjoy the agreed investment benefits. Yiwu Yongxin Company therefore requested that the court dismiss Wanshun Company's claims.

During the proceedings at first instance, upon the application of Wanshun Company and with the consent of the other two parties, the court of first instance, on May 15, 2001, commissioned Zhejiang Jiangnan Certified Public Accountants (hereinafter referred to as Jiangnan Firm) to audit the investment, expenditure, and profit of the approximately 80,000 square meter plot of the original Yiwu Paper Mill jointly developed by Wanshun Company and Yongxin Company. On September 18, Jiangnan Firm issued a draft audit report. On the same day and the following day, the court of first instance served the draft audit report to Wanshun Company, Yiwu Yongxin Company, and Yongxin Company. On September 25, under the auspices of the court of first instance, Jiangnan Firm and the three parties conducted a line-by-line verification of the disputed items. On December 7, Jiangnan Firm issued the formal report, confirming the net profit to be RMB 58,170,400. The report also noted that, according to the supplementary agreement between Wanshun Company and Yongxin Company dated June 10, 1993, the RMB 12 million invested in the printing enterprise was to be included in the land cost. However, this cost arrangement was inconsistent with tax policies, and therefore the audit did not deduct it as a cost. Whether it should be deducted from the net profit was to be determined by the court.

The court of first instance further found that the annual inspection materials of Yiwu Yongxin Company for 1995 and 1996, issued by Yiwu Administration for Industry and Commerce, showed that the owner's equity was RMB 10 million in both years. The audit report of Shanghai Huangpu Gongrui Accounting Firm stated that Wanshun Company was a wholly-owned subsidiary of Yiwu Velvet Chemical General Factory and that Wanshun Company had no investment projects in Yiwu real estate. On May 11, 1994, Yiwu Yongxin Company borrowed RMB 20 million from Yiwu Industrial and Commercial Bank.

The court of first instance, upon trial, held that according to the claims and defenses of both parties, the issues in dispute in this case were: 1. the nature of the RMB 10 million payment; 2. whether the cooperation agreement had been terminated; 3. whether the statute of limitations had expired for the claims in this case; and 4. how to divide the profits.

Regarding the nature of the RMB 10 million payment. Based on the remittance voucher of April 14, 1993, the contents of the agreement and supplementary agreement signed by both parties on May 4 and June 10 of the same year, and the financing from Yangming Company by Wanshun Company in December of the same year, it was clear that the RMB 10 million was an investment. There was currently no evidence that Yongxin Company and Wanshun Company had reached an agreement to convert this payment into a loan. Wanshun Company's ground for this claim was established, and the objections of Yongxin Company and Yiwu Yongxin Company were not sustainable.

Regarding whether the cooperation agreement had been terminated. Pursuant to Article 26 of the original Economic Contract Law of the PRC, "The modification or rescission of an economic contract is permitted under any of the following circumstances: (1) the parties have mutually agreed and such modification or rescission does not harm the interests of the state or the public; (2) a force majeure event makes it impossible to perform all obligations under the economic contract; (3) the other party fails to perform the contract within the agreed period. In the circumstances described in items (2) or (3) of the preceding paragraph, one party has the right to notify the other party of the rescission of the contract. If a party suffers losses due to the modification or rescission of an economic contract, the responsible party shall compensate for such losses, except where liability is exempted by law." The key issue was whether Wanshun Company had failed to perform the contract within the agreed period. Article 3 of the agreement of May 4, 1993 stipulated: "Party B (Wanshun Company) shall be responsible for raising funds and, in accordance with the contract and relevant agreements signed between Party A (Yongxin Company) and Yiwu Land Administration Bureau, pay all land prices (payment method shall be according to the time specified in the relevant contract)." Article 4 stipulated: "Party B shall, in accordance with relevant regulations, bear the costs for leveling and providing utilities, greening, community road construction, and water and electricity capacity expansion within the transferred land parcel." According to these two articles, Wanshun Company was responsible for paying the land transfer fee and costs for leveling and utilities. Pursuant to Article 2, Item 7 of the "State-Owned Land Use Rights Transfer Contract" of August 2, 1993, "When both parties sign the State-Owned Land Use Rights Transfer Contract, Party B (Yiwu Yongxin Company) must pay Party A (Yiwu Land Administration Bureau) a deposit totaling RMB 10 million, pay another RMB 20 million within two months from the date of signing the land use rights transfer contract, and pay the remaining land price in full within six months from the date of signing the contract... If payment is not made in full within the time limit, Party A has the right to rescind the contract, the deposit shall not be refunded, and Party A has the right to claim compensation for breach of contract." Accordingly, Wanshun Company should have paid the land transfer fee and costs for leveling and utilities in full by February 1, 1994. Wanshun Company's failure to pay within that period constituted a breach of contract. Although the former director of Yiwu Land Administration Bureau, Zhu Hai, testified that Yiwu Yongxin Company paid the deposit of RMB 10 million for the land transfer fee, and the second installment was basically paid on time; thereafter, Yiwu Yongxin Company claimed that part of the transferred land area was occupied by public buildings and requested a re-measurement of the area before paying the full transfer fee; after the Land Administration Bureau verified the area and confirmed this fact, it did not pursue liability for the delayed payment. However, this only indicated that there was no breach between Yiwu Yongxin Company and Yiwu Land Administration Bureau; it did not mean that Wanshun Company's failure to pay did not constitute a breach. Moreover, Wanshun Company subsequently still failed to perform its obligations under the agreement and never paid the land transfer fee and costs for leveling and utilities, constituting a fundamental breach. Yongxin Company had the right to rescind the contract according to the provisions of the aforementioned Economic Contract Law. On April 1, 1994, Yongxin Company had notified Wanshun Company in writing and granted a 15-day extension period. Wanshun Company still failed to perform its obligations within that time. The cooperation and development agreement between the parties had been rescinded. Yongxin Company's defense that the agreement of May 4, 1993 had been rescinded was established.

Regarding whether the statute of limitations had expired for the claims in this case. The agreement of May 4, 1993 had been rescinded, but the entire development project had not yet concluded. The claim for profits had not exceeded the statute of limitations. Whether profits could be distributed was a substantive issue. The arguments of Yongxin Company and Yiwu Yongxin Company that the claims in this case had exceeded the statute of limitations were not sustainable.

Regarding how to divide the profits. The agreement of May 4, 1993 and the supplementary agreement of June 10, 1993 had been rescinded. Rescission has retroactive effect to the time of the agreement's formation, eliminating the agreement from its inception. Thus, debts not yet performed are extinguished, and for anything already given, a claim for restitution arises. Wanshun Company's RMB 10 million had only been with Yongxin Company for a little over three months. Restitution would only require payment of interest. On January 13, 1994, Yiwu Yongxin Company paid Wanshun Company interest of RMB 200,000. Calculated according to bank loan interest rates, this amount covered both the interest on RMB 6 million for one month and the interest on RMB 10 million for over three months. Therefore, Wanshun Company's rights had already been protected.

In summary, regarding the agreement signed by Wanshun Company and Yongxin Company on May 4, 1993, given that Wanshun Company was a real estate development company, it met the qualification requirements of Article 1 of the Supreme People's Court's "Answers on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Real Estate Development and Operation Cases Arising Before the Implementation of the Real Estate Administration Law," which states: "Persons engaged in real estate development and operation shall be real estate development enterprises that meet the conditions of a legal person enterprise, registered with the administrative department for industry and commerce and issued a business license." Thereafter, the parties established Yiwu Yongxin Company pursuant to the agreement, and the land use rights were registered under the name of Yiwu Yongxin Company. The agreement had been substantially performed, and the buildings had been constructed. Therefore, the agreement should be confirmed as valid. Wanshun Company's failure to pay the land transfer fee and costs for leveling and utilities as agreed constituted a fundamental breach. According to Article 26 of the original Economic Contract Law of the PRC, Yongxin Company had the right to rescind. On April 1, 1994, Yongxin Company exercised that right. Therefore, the agreement between Wanshun Company and Yongxin Company had been rescinded. Since rescission has retroactive effect, the agreement is treated as if it never existed. Wanshun Company's claim for a share of profits lacked contractual and legal basis and was not legally sustainable. Accordingly, the court dismissed Wanshun Company's claims. Court costs of RMB 140,860, property preservation costs of RMB 81,670, appraisal fees of RMB 2,000, and audit fees of RMB 340,000, totaling RMB 582,530, were to be borne by Wanshun Company.

Wanshun Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed, arguing: 1. The first-instance court erred in finding that the agreement signed on May 4, 1993 had been rescinded. The parties had been performing the cooperation agreement continuously until the lawsuit was filed, and it had not been rescinded; 2. The first-instance judgment erred in dismissing Wanshun Company's claim for distribution of profits on the ground that the cooperation agreement had been rescinded. Wanshun Company had the right to a 45% share of the profits of RMB 58,170,400, totaling RMB 26,170,000, according to the terms of the cooperation agreement. Therefore, it requested this Court to set aside the first-instance judgment, order Yongxin Company to pay Wanshun Company RMB 26,170,000 in profits from the cooperative real estate development, and bear the litigation costs of both instances.

Yongxin Company argued in defense: 1. The RMB 10 million remitted by Wanshun Company to the respondent was a loan. This amount, along with interest, had already been recovered by Wanshun Company before the establishment of Yiwu Yongxin Company. Therefore, Wanshun Company had no right to share investment profits based on this loan; 2. Even if the RMB 10 million was an investment, it had already been recovered by Wanshun Company. Wanshun Company failed to perform its obligations under the parties' cooperation agreement, causing significant difficulties in the financial and operational functioning of Yiwu Yongxin Company, thereby losing the basis for cooperation. Its actions constituted a fundamental breach. The respondent exercised its right to rescind the contract in accordance with the law, and the cooperative relationship between the parties terminated on April 16, 1994. Wanshun Company still had no right to demand a share of profits under the agreement; 3. After the rescission of the cooperation agreement, Wanshun Company never performed its obligations under the agreement, never exercised its shareholder rights, and had no shareholder interest in Yiwu Yongxin Company. Therefore, it requested this Court to dismiss Wanshun Company's appeal and uphold the original judgment.

Yiwu Yongxin Company argued in defense: 1. The RMB 10 million remitted by Wanshun Company on April 14, 1993 was a loan. Even if it were deemed an investment, Wanshun Company had already recovered the funds on August 7, 1993; 2. Wanshun Company failed to fulfill its capital contribution obligations and should bear liability for breach of contract. Its claim that project funds were sufficient and could be rolled over from pre-sale proceeds was not factual; 3. The parties' cooperation agreement had been lawfully rescinded on April 16, 1994. Therefore, it requested the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment upheld.

The Court of Second Instance further found that on August 2, 1993, the Yiwu Land Administration Bureau and Yongxin Company signed a land use rights transfer contract with the same date, document number, and content as that signed with Yiwu Yongxin Company. According to the second-instance trial, the contract for the transfer of state-owned land use rights between Yiwu Yongxin Company and the Yiwu Land Administration Bureau was backdated. At the time of the backdating, Yiwu Yongxin Company had not yet been established. The approval certificate for the establishment of Yiwu Yongxin Company issued by the Zhejiang Provincial Department of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation and the business license of Yiwu Yongxin Company as a legal person enterprise both stated: The investor of Yiwu Yongxin Company was Yongxin Company, with a total investment of USD 6 million, a registered capital of USD 3 million, and the investor's capital contribution of USD 3 million. The audit report issued by Jiangnan Certified Public Accountants stated that in the cooperative project, the Hong Kong City Building, the garage behind Building A, the kindergarten building (to be built), the additional building for the neighborhood committee, and the northern 5 buildings had not yet been sold; therefore, income and costs were not included in the income statement, and costs were recorded as development costs. The audit report also stated that on April 22, 1993, the Beijing Office of Yongxin Company remitted RMB 10 million to the Yiwu Real Estate Management Office for investment purposes. The office issued a receipt for "prepaid land transfer fees" of RMB 10 million to Yongxin Company on May 4 of the same year. On January 28, 1994, based on the above information, the Yiwu Audit Firm issued Verification Report No. (1994) 10, confirming that Yiwu Yongxin Company's actual contributed capital was RMB 10 million. Apart from the above, no other capital contribution records were found in Yiwu Yongxin Company's accounting records. The registered capital of USD 3 million indicated in the business license was not contributed in foreign currency. Yongxin Company also did not contribute the total investment of USD 6 million as stated in the approval certificate for the establishment of Yiwu Yongxin Company issued by the Zhejiang Provincial Department of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation and the business license of Yiwu Yongxin Company. This Court found the other facts to be the same as those found by the first-instance court.

This Court holds that there are four issues in dispute in this case: 1. The nature and validity of the cooperation agreement signed between Wanshun Company and Yongxin Company; 2. The nature of the RMB 10 million contributed by Wanshun Company; 3. Whether the cooperation agreement has been rescinded; 4. The distribution of profits from the cooperative project.

Regarding the nature and validity of the cooperation agreement between the parties. From the contents of the agreement and supplementary agreement signed on May 4 and June 10, 1993, Yongxin Company's contractual obligations were: to secure the cooperative project and the transfer of land use rights, handle the preliminary procedures required for the development project, and establish the project company in its own name. Wanshun Company's obligations were: to raise funds to pay all land prices stipulated in the land transfer contract for the parcel, as well as costs for leveling and utilities, greening, community road construction, and water and electricity capacity expansion; to send personnel to participate in the management of the project company and be fully responsible for financial work. The profit distribution ratio agreed upon by the parties in the cooperation agreement was for the entire real estate development project. Although Yiwu Yongxin Company was a wholly foreign-owned enterprise established by Yongxin Company, it was established to operate the parties' cooperative project. Therefore, the relationship between the parties should be characterized as a project cooperation relationship, and the cooperation agreement signed by the parties should be characterized as a project cooperation agreement. Since the cooperation between the parties did not result, at the final level, in the establishment of a Sino-foreign equity joint venture or a Sino-foreign contractual joint venture, the cooperation agreement signed by the parties does not fall within the category of joint venture or contractual joint venture contracts that require approval to be established or become effective under laws or administrative regulations. This cooperation agreement does not violate any prohibitive provisions of laws or administrative regulations and should be deemed valid.

Regarding the nature of the RMB 10 million contributed by Wanshun Company. Although Yiwu Yongxin Company recorded this payment as "short-term loan" in the accounting voucher of October 31, 1993, this accounting entry was made internally by the enterprise. Yongxin Company's assertion that this RMB 10 million was a loan lacks sufficient evidentiary basis. If the RMB 10 million contributed by Wanshun Company were a loan rather than an investment, then the remittance of RMB 10 million from Yiwu Yongxin Company on August 7, 1993 should have been characterized as a repayment of the loan. The purpose of a lender providing a loan is to obtain interest on the loan. However, the interest on this RMB 10 million was actually remitted by Wanshun Company in advance to Yiwu Yongxin Company's account. This sequence of actions indicates that the RMB 10 million contributed by Wanshun Company was not a loan. Considering the contents of the parties' cooperation agreement, Wanshun Company's dispatch of personnel to participate in the management of Yiwu Yongxin Company, and the fact that Yongxin Company sent a letter on April 1, 1994 requiring Wanshun Company to fulfill the obligation to contribute funds under the cooperation agreement, characterizing this amount as an investment is consistent both with the facts proven by the existing evidence and with the true expression of intent reflected in the series of actions of the parties. Therefore, the RMB 10 million contributed by Wanshun Company should be characterized as an investment.

Regarding whether the cooperation agreement between the parties has been rescinded. According to Article 1, Paragraph 2 of the Supreme People's Court's "Answers on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Foreign Economic Contract Law of the PRC," disputes arising from contracts between Chinese (mainland) enterprise legal persons and legal persons of enterprises from Hong Kong and Macao, unless the parties have expressly chosen to apply the original Economic Contract Law of the PRC, should be governed by the original Foreign Economic Contract Law of the PRC. The parties' cooperation agreement did not expressly choose to apply the original Economic Contract Law of the PRC. Therefore, the first-instance court's reliance on the original Economic Contract Law of the PRC as the basis for determining whether the cooperation agreement had been rescinded constituted an error in the application of law and should be corrected. The content of the "April 1 letter" sent by Yongxin Company to Wanshun Company was twofold: (1) Requesting Wanshun Company to remit RMB 78,975,000 for the land transfer fee and various costs totaling over RMB 8,000,000 for leveling and utilities, etc., to Yiwu Yongxin Company before April 15; (2) If the funds were not remitted to the designated bank on time, it would be deemed that Wanshun Company had unilaterally rescinded the agreement. Article 29(2) and Article 32 of the original Foreign Economic Contract Law of the PRC provide that if the other party fails to perform the contract within the agreed period and still fails to perform within a reasonable period allowed for postponed performance, one party has the right to notify the other party to rescind the contract. The notice of rescission shall be in written form. Considering the content of the "April 1 letter" and the provisions of the above legal articles, Yongxin Company could only have the right to rescind the contract if Wanshun Company still failed to perform its contractual obligations within the reasonable extension period allowed for postponed performance. When Yongxin Company issued the "April 1 letter," the grace period had not yet expired, so Yongxin Company did not yet have the right to rescind the contract. After Wanshun Company failed to perform its cooperation obligations beyond the grace period, Yongxin Company could not prove that the telegram rescinding the contract had reached Wanshun Company. Therefore, it is difficult to prove the legal fact of the exercise of the right of rescission. Furthermore, according to the parties' cooperation agreement, Yongxin Company had an obligation to establish, in its own name, a real estate development company for the cooperative project in Yiwu. In performing this agreement, although Yongxin Company established the real estate development company, it did not pay the registered capital to that company, nor did it make investments according to the total investment amount. According to Article 9 of the Law of the PRC on Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprises and Articles 18, 19, and 20 of the Implementing Rules for the Law of the PRC on Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprises, Yongxin Company failed to fulfill the obligations stipulated by the above laws and administrative regulations. The company it established could not be considered full performance of the cooperation agreement. From the perspective of Yongxin Company's own obligations under the cooperation agreement, it should be determined that Yongxin Company had already breached the contract. Since the purpose of the contract rescission system is to grant the right of rescission to the non-breaching party, and Yongxin Company was still in breach when it issued the "April 1 letter," Yongxin Company cannot enjoy the right to rescind the contract. Given that the legal facts for the rescission of the parties' cooperation agreement have not yet been established, the first-instance court's finding that the cooperation agreement had been rescinded was erroneous and should be corrected.

Regarding the distribution of profits from the cooperative project. The relationship between Wanshun Company and Yongxin Company is a project cooperation relationship. Since the parties' cooperation agreement does not provide for phased profit distribution, the distribution of profits from the cooperative project should be conducted after the entire cooperative project is fully completed and settled. In this case, the audit report commissioned by the first-instance court from the appraisal institution stated that among the parties' cooperative project, the Hong Kong City Building, the garage behind Building A, the kindergarten building (to be built), the additional building for the neighborhood committee, and the northern 5 buildings had not yet been sold and were not included in the income statement. The parties' cooperative project has not been fully completed, and the final profit or loss conclusion for the entire cooperative project cannot be determined. Under these circumstances, Wanshun Company's claim for distribution of cooperative profits has no contractual basis. Since Wanshun Company insists that the cooperation agreement has not been rescinded and has not filed a claim for rescission, there is no legal basis for this Court to order phased profit distribution.

Based on the above facts and reasons, this Court holds that although the project cooperation agreement signed by Wanshun Company and Yongxin Company is valid, the RMB 10 million contributed by Wanshun Company is an investment rather than a loan, and the cooperation agreement between the parties remains binding on both parties to date, because the cooperative project between the parties has not yet been fully completed, Wanshun Company's claim for phased profit distribution has no contractual or legal basis and should be dismissed. Although the first-instance judgment also dismissed Wanshun Company's claims, the facts, reasons, and applicable law on which it was based were erroneous and should be set aside. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Items (2) and (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 19 of the Supreme People's Court's "Measures on Litigation Cost Payment," the judgment is as follows:

Set aside the original judgment and dismiss all claims of Shanghai Wanshun Real Estate Development Corporation.

The litigation costs of the first instance shall be borne as determined in the first-instance judgment. The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 140,860 shall be borne by Shanghai Wanshun Real Estate Development Corporation.

This judgment is final.
